title: agents_Inc: A Model Ladder for Delegating and Verifying Work Across AI Agents
description:
agents_Inc is a governed multi-agent dispatch and verification layer. It pools Claude, Codex, Gemini, Mistral and OpenRouter capacity behind one launcher, agents-inc, so a supervising agent can hand work to cheaper or specialised models without paying for a new API.

You name models in plain English. A four-rung ladder (Executive, Orchestrator, Workhorse, Grunt) decides who manages whom, and every dispatch carries a 14-element prompt contract. A delegate never grades its own work: output passes deterministic checks, then a reviewer, and each decision lands in an append-only ledger.

Main features

  • One command, agents-inc dispatch, for Claude and Codex delegates, with prompt linting, a pre-run snapshot of the working tree and a verdict on return.
  • Sandboxed Codex delegates that work like Claude subagents: tools, scoped write access, skills and built-in image generation.
  • Model sync that detects new Claude and Codex models and promotes them with approval or pins.
  • A credential-blind broker for nested runs, and a ledger that records every launched dispatch.
  • Standard library only at runtime. Install with pip install agents-inc, then agents-inc install.

New in 0.3.1

  • Opt-in network access for Codex delegates: the slot CODEX_NETWORK: yes or agents-inc run --network. Off by default.
  • Codex tool commands get a private writable temp directory, so heredocs and scratch files work.
  • A dispatched Codex delegate can run its own snapshot check.
  • The snapshot check accepts allowed files inside a new directory.
  • agents-inc report bug|feature drafts a GitHub issue; --submit files it.
  • Sessions and agents-inc doctor say when a newer release is on PyPI.

The full change list is in CHANGELOG.md. The project is experimental; the governed path is off by default.

How to cite

If you use agents_Inc in research or in published work, please cite it:

Mattioli, D. O. (2026). agents_Inc: A Model Ladder for Delegating and Verifying Work Across AI Agents (Version 0.3.1) [Computer software]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22670100

The DOI above covers all versions. GitHub's "Cite this repository" button reads CITATION.cff.
